summary: Erich Haenisch worked in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube, Richard Pischel, and Jules Oppert, and held professorships at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Munich (1927–1951).

Philosopher Erich Heintel earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he served as associate professor (1952) and full professor (1960–1982). He also became a full member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1978.
Indologist Erich Herold studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. in 1947 under Oldřich Friš and Vincenc Lesný. He served as director of the Náprstek Museum from 1959 to 1970.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen (~1905–1909) and habilitated at Strasbourg, later serving as professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and the University of Marburg from 1913.
Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Erich Wolff studied at the University of Hamburg and Heidelberg University (1924–1930), completing his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Max Walleser.

Erich von Voss worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1900–1904) and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig (~1904–1906), later serving as a teacher of German and Greek at Petrischule.

Erik Braun specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso and teachers Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun; his posts include Harvard (attested 2010) and faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. His academic career included appointments at Harvard University (~1933–1936), the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960).

Erik Gren studied classical history and archaeology at Uppsala University (~1923–1941). He was appointed assistant librarian at Uppsala University Library in 1931 and privatdozent of classical history at Uppsala University in 1941.

Erik Haarh specialized in Tibetology, religious studies, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library, the University of Copenhagen, and Aarhus University, where he became professor of the history of religions.

Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

Linguist Erik Johan Tammelin studied at the University of Helsinki and under Berthold Delbrück at the University of Jena. He served the National Board of Education as chief inspector of classical languages (1894) and secondary schools department head (1918).
Erik Pema Kunsang is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (~1981) and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark (~2004).

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar Erik Zürcher completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1947–1959) and studied under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, Édouard Chavannes, and J.J.L. Duyvendak. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the University of Amsterdam (1993–1997), Leiden University (from 1997), and served as director of the International Institute of Social History (2008–2012).

Erika Forte specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She served as a research associate at Ruhr University Bochum (2018–2019) and as a professor at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2026).
Erika Sandman works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Helsinki (2007–2016) and later held a post there.

Sinologist Erling von Mende studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, completing his Ph.D. (1969) and habilitation (1979) at Cologne. In 1983, he was appointed professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin, serving until 2007.

Indologist and linguist Ermenegildo La Terza studied under Michele Kerbaker at the University of Naples Federico II. He taught Latin literature at the University of Messina (1923–1924) and Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Naples (1904; 1925–1935).
Ernest Arthur Gardner was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884) and later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.
